changes: Reconstruct definition/history events from retained original responses and observations; compare derived requests, definitions, revisions and action links instead of trusting edited summaries.

Preserve exact initial/revised definition text, raw-response linkage and genuinely later issued SQL. Event replay does not certify SQL execution, billing, archive authenticity or semantic correctness.
Require all twelve conditions before constructing review drafts. Invalid model outputs stay in coverage; unfinished or failed histories are refused rather than scored as correct or removed.

Build two unfilled reviewer packets. Stage A shows current task and exact initial definition only; Stage B contains preceding definitions and subsequent issued programs and must be withheld until both Stage A reviews are locked.

Keep condition mapping and coverage private; ordinary workflows without elicited definitions remain unassessed. Exact model wording can reveal condition, so masking is partial rather than guaranteed blinding.
